root_motivation: WHO: the coding agent in Claude Code reading the plugin skill first, and the maintainer who ships a verb and forgets the skill. WHAT: a skill whose verbs, plan ceilings, error remedies and local-loop commands are rendered from the host's own registries. WHY: the skill is hand-written, names six of 535 tool entries, states no ceiling and no error code, so an agent sends a call the host refuses.
user_persona: A coding agent that reads plugin/skills/mcphost/SKILL.md, finds the family a verb lives in, reads the free ceilings before it calls, and looks up the remedy for an error code it hit; and the maintainer whose cargo test fails until `mcphost skill-gen --write` is run.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the registry, When `mcphost skill-gen --section verbs` renders, Then every dotted family has exactly one line with its count and verb names, the 11 anonymous starter verbs are named, no per-verb description appears, and the section is at most 60 lines.
Given the checked-in files, When `mcphost skill-gen` runs without `--write`, Then it exits 0; Given one line edited by hand inside a marked section, Then it exits 1 and names the line.
Given a new `Tool::new("host.example")` added to `host_tools`, When `cargo test` runs, Then the drift test fails until `skill-gen --write` regenerates and the new verb appears under its family.

Given `ERROR_CODES` gains an entry, When `cargo test` runs, Then the drift test fails until the skill is regenerated, and a remedy that names a verb absent from `host_tools` fails the remedy test naming the code.

Given the `limits` section, When rendered, Then every key of `plan.ceilings_json()` for `free` appears with its value and no number in the section is typed outside the generator (test: the section's numbers equal the JSON's).
Given a binary built without the `dev` or `push` subcommands, When `skill-gen` renders `devloop`, Then the section says `no local verbs in this build` for the absent verbs and names none of them.

Given `--url <the mcp url of a running host> --section verbs` against a local test host, When rendered, Then the output is derived from that host's `tools/list` and differs from the registry render only by verbs not yet deployed.

Given prod, When `diff <(curl -s https://mcphost.dev/skill.md | sed -n '/mcphost-verbs:start/,/mcphost-verbs:end/p') <(mcphost skill-gen --section verbs --url https://mcphost.dev/mcp | sed -n '/mcphost-verbs:start/,/mcphost-verbs:end/p')` runs, Then it prints nothing and exits 0 (Live; evidence: that command's exit code and empty stdout)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: that command's exit code and empty stdout)

scope: src/skill_gen.rs (renderers for verbs, limits, errors, devloop; splice, check, tools/list fetch); src/main.rs (SkillGen subcommand); src/handler.rs (starter_tool_names); plugin/skills/mcphost/SKILL.md and www/skill.md (four marked sections); scripts/skill-gen-check.sh; remedy texts in src/org.rs, src/errors.rs, src/subkeys.rs, src/notify.rs, src/email_send.rs, src/drift/review.rs that named a verb the host does not serve.
non_goals: Rewriting the hand-written narrative; generating README.md or llms.txt; per-client skills; a second remedy table; the plugin.json version bump (R8, P1, wm-build land bumps); the Recipes section (R9, P2); the AC 8 prod diff (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.one_render_path: Every section is rendered by src/skill_gen.rs; no number, verb or code is typed in the skill outside a marked block.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent send calls the host refuses?
five_whys_trace.a: The skill it reads first states no ceiling, no error code and names six verbs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the skill omit them?
five_whys_trace.a: It is hand-written; only two blocks are generated.

five_whys_trace.q: Why were the other facts never generated?
five_whys_trace.a: No generator reads the verb, plan and error registries into the skill.
Nothing fails when a verb ships and the skill is not updated.
There was no drift test over the skill; skill-gen plus the skgn drift test add one.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The PRD says 11 anonymous starter verbs; which set is named?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The registry's own anonymous starter listing (starter_tools: signup plus 17 host.*/billing.* names), read through handler::starter_tool_names; the count in the PRD is the stale comment above STARTER_TOOL_NAMES.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does --url need a key?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: An anonymous tools/list is only the starter set, so --url takes --key or MCPHOST_TENANT_KEY and refuses an anonymous starter-only listing.
